node.question: Using s1's inventory, what visible boundary evidence establishes paper entry or excludes it across all relevant paper–receiver contact regions, and which specific regions remain unresolved?
node.criteria: Pass if a grounded boundary assessment can be reported, including unresolved relations. Fail only if adequate visibility establishes absence of the paper or any possible receiver. Unknown if visibility prevents a grounded assessment. In the evidence, separately report receiver identity (cup/non-cup/unresolved), relation (entry/wholly external/rim-only/unresolved), requested progress (established/excluded/unresolved), and completion (established/excluded/unresolved). For wholly external placement, supply an exclusion certificate: identify the paper extent assessed, every relevant hidden contact region, and the affirmative geometry that excludes entry at each region. A visible foreground edge, no visible opening, or no observed disappearing segment is not by itself such a certificate. If any relevant region remains undecidable, relation is unresolved rather than wholly external. Positive requested entry requires established cup identity. Conversely, entry excluded into every candidate receiver establishes no requested insertion progress even if receiver identity is unresolved. Mapping success itself earns no progress or completion credit.
node.binding: Consume s1 as coarse ancestor context, then inspect the edited image directly. Map visible paper edges and candidate receiver boundaries with relative locations, overlap ordering, and the scope of each observation. For each hidden paper segment, identify its occluder and visible endpoints where available. Distinguish an occluded paper edge from a receiver surface or possible opening hidden behind the paper. When considering wholly external placement, test whether the stated evidence excludes entry anywhere relevant, rather than merely showing one exposed region in front. When considering unresolved entry, name the actual localized ambiguity and explain why visible geometry does not settle it; do not rely on generic hand occlusion or purely imagined hidden geometry. Report missing exclusion evidence honestly without inventing an entry path. Assess curved lines from visible structure without presuming they are rims or markings. Do not assume colors, source correspondence, or cup identity. Return the boundary assessment, exclusion certificate or its specific evidentiary gap, and separately typed findings as evidence within the saved checker response format.

dependencies.evidence: Source: a large white sheet of paper is visible beside a blue cup lying on its side; the cup has a broad oval opening and enclosing cylindrical walls. Edited: a blue printed paper/card is held in a hand, with its boundaries mostly visible. A reddish rounded object behind it has a curved outer contour and a dark line across it, but the image does not show enough structure to identify it as a cup or establish correspondence with the source cup. The paper overlaps and obscures part of that object's front; the hand also covers part of the paper. The images allow a grounded inventory and comparison, while edited receiving-object identity and source-to-edit correspondence remain unresolved.
